scope: Definition-PR security verdict for release v0.4.5 (feature/0.4.5 -> develop, milestone (a)). Diff-based review of origin/main..199b356b: 4 commits, docs/specs only — backlog materialization, archive sweep (git mv of one v0.4.4 verdict), and the SPEC/PLAN/TASKS definition + BACKLOG purge + ACTIVE flip + superseded event. Zero production code, zero dependency manifest, zero CI/IaC in the delta. Live-tree placement because specs/_archive is FROZEN.
verdict_reason: The delta is authored specs prose only and carries no blocking security or privacy finding: six pattern sweeps over the 2065 added lines return zero hits (secret assignments, PEM key blocks, home-absolute paths, email literals, IPv4/host literals, cloud key prefixes), the refspec-fed push gate runs the operator denylist + baseline over the real new-branch range and exits 0 with zero offenders, and the repo self-scan passes 5/5. The design spot-check confirms the release strengthens rather than weakens the security surface: FR6 makes the operator denylist a single loading seam consumed by both the write-time redaction and the push-time scan with A6.3 pinning the push-time scan unchanged in behaviour ('complements, never replaces') and A6.4 keeping the denylist data out of public/**; FR7 closes CWE-117 plus a silent-event-loss path at one seam with A7.4 forbidding any historical rewrite; FR8 extends the CWE-59 refusal posture without new vocabulary. Section 2.4 records the no-publish ADR against operator order O5 honestly, naming the one-axis tension rather than hiding it, and A16.8 makes it mechanically verifiable (approve job pending-unapproved, no v0.4.5 tag, PyPI latest still 0.4.4) — a supply-chain-positive posture. Two non-blocking findings (one MEDIUM, one LOW) are design constraints on code that does not yet exist; both are prescriptions the S1/S3 implementation reviews must enforce, not defects of this diff. Routing: the MEDIUM (FR1 manifest-sourced LAW class) is carried into S1 as an added acceptance A1.7 before FR1 is coded, and the LOW (FR6/FR7 runtime ordering) into S3 as an added acceptance A7.6; both are prescriptions on unwritten code and neither blocks this PR.

findings.message: FR1 sources the fail-closed LAW class partly from .dadaia/agentic/manifest.json, which classifies UNGATED on the executed path — an agent can demote a projected law file to MUTATING by editing the manifest, then edit the law. Prescribe a fail-closed floor before implementation.
findings.detail_md:
**Where.** `specs/releases/v0.4.5/SPEC.md:210-214` (FR1's predicate): *"a path is LAW when it is the workspace-root law family (`DADAIA.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` at the root) **or** it is listed in `.dadaia/agentic/manifest.json` as a lib-originated projection."*

**Why it matters.** Current product truth (`specs/memory/product/sdd/sdd-gate-v3.md:69`) states the class contract: *"PROTECTED | Session identity records and projected law files are fail-closed."* Today that fail-closed set is **static** — `dadaia_workspace/core/workspace_layout.py:48,53` pin `LAW_BASENAMES` and `LAW_HARNESS_DIRS`, and `features/spec_context/gate_policy.py:256-269` matches against those frozensets with no file read. FR1 replaces the harness-dir arm of that static floor with a lookup into a file that the gate itself does not protect.

**Executed-path evidence** (`classify_path` called directly, not inferred):

```
.dadaia/agentic/manifest.json            -> UNGATED
.claude/rules/DADAIA.md                  -> LAW
DADAIA.md                                -> LAW
repos/x/AGENTS.md                        -> LAW      <- the over-match FR1 correctly fixes
.dadaia/sessions/a.json                  -> PROTECTED
```

`_PROTECTED_PREFIX` is `.dadaia/sessions/` alone (`gate_policy.py:80`) and `DADAIA_ADDITIVE_PREFIXES` covers only `.dadaia/{reports,handoff,tmp}/` (`workspace_layout.py:41-45`), so `.dadaia/agentic/manifest.json` falls through to `UNGATED` — writable by any agent with a file tool, with no gate decision at all.

**The gap.** Post-FR1, the sequence `Write .dadaia/agentic/manifest.json` (removing an entry) then `Edit .claude/rules/DADAIA.md` classifies MUTATING and proceeds — a self-service bypass of a class DADAIA.md §8 reserves for a human operator (CWE-284: security decision relies on data outside the trust boundary; the manifest becomes untrusted input to an access-control decision). A1.3's contract test enumerates the manifest as it stands at test time, so it proves the mapping is honoured — it cannot prove the mapping is tamper-resistant at runtime.

**This is a design constraint, not a defect of this diff.** The reviewed delta contains no code and changes no gate behaviour; the risk materializes only if FR1 lands as literally worded.

**Precedent for the prescription.** The same atom already rejects exactly this shape one section down (`sdd-gate-v3.md:72-79`): the MEMORY dotfile carve-out was refused because it *"would open an always-writable hole under the MEMORY prefix through which curated lint canon could mutate mid-implementation, which is the stale-layer pattern the gate exists to prevent."* A manifest-sourced LAW set is that same hole, one class over.
findings.fix_recommendation: Make the manifest arm **additive-only** — the cheapest option, and the one that adds no branch (standing order: the fix must not grow the feature). Keep the existing static floor (`LAW_BASENAMES` at the workspace root **and** at `LAW_HARNESS_DIRS`) as an unconditional LAW match, and let the manifest lookup only **extend** LAW to further projections — never remove a path from it. FR1's two RED cases (A1.1/A1.2: `repos/<slug>/AGENTS.md`, fresh or existing) still flip to MUTATING, because the repo arm is where the basename over-match lives (`gate_policy.py:263-264`), and that arm is deleted outright — so the fix stays net-negative in `gate_policy.py` as A1.4 requires. Then add one acceptance to FR1: *A1.7 — removing an entry from `.dadaia/agentic/manifest.json` does not demote any statically-floored law path out of LAW, proven on the executed path.* If instead the manifest is to be authoritative, classify `.dadaia/agentic/manifest.json` PROTECTED in the same commit and make an unreadable/missing manifest fail **closed** (treat law basenames at projection dirs as LAW) rather than open.

findings.message: FR6 and FR7 share the bug-event seam but no acceptance pins their RUNTIME order; redact-then-sanitize lets a control-character-interrupted denylisted term evade the FR6 redaction and be normalized back into the ledger by FR7.
findings.detail_md:
**Where.** `specs/releases/v0.4.5/SPEC.md:332-374` (FR6, FR7) and `specs/releases/v0.4.5/PLAN.md:162-163`.

The PLAN pins the **implementation** order — *"FR6 and FR7 both touch the bug ledger and are sequenced FR6 → FR7 so the redaction seam is settled before the sanitation pass wraps it"* — which is about which FR lands first. Neither FR's acceptance pins the order the two passes run **at write time**, and after both land they sit on the same seam.

**The vector.** If redaction runs on the raw field and sanitation runs after it, a free-text value carrying a denylisted term interrupted by an ESC or U+2028 (`sec<U+2028>ret`) does not match FR6's term patterns, passes redaction unmasked, and is then normalized by FR7's sanitation pass into the clean term — written to `specs/bugs/bugs.jsonl` in the clear. FR6's own premise is that this class already cost two committed leaks in v0.4.4, one forcing an `rc-1` history rewrite; the push gate would still catch the committed result at push time (`sdd-gate-v3.md:395-410`), so the failure mode is a repeat of the expensive late catch FR6 exists to eliminate, not an unbounded leak.

Severity is LOW: it needs an adversarially- or accidentally-shaped field value, and the push-time scan remains as the backstop A6.3 explicitly preserves.
findings.fix_recommendation: Add one acceptance to FR7 fixing the runtime order at the single seam: *A7.6 — sanitation runs **before** redaction, so the redaction pass sees normalized text; proven by a fixture whose field carries a denylisted term interrupted by U+2028 and by one carrying it interrupted by ESC, both masked in the written record.* This costs one ordering line and two fixture cases inside the one seam FR7 already builds — no new branch, no second guard, consistent with A7.3.

findings.message: Section 2.4's no-publish ADR states operator order O5 explicitly, rejects 'publish anyway because the pipeline is automated', and is made mechanically verifiable by A16.8 — an honest and supply-chain-positive posture.
findings.detail_md:
Spot-check requested by the dispatch. `SPEC.md:139-160` decides the release id is `v0.4.5` with `pyproject.toml` bumping at the final `rc` per the one-axis law, and states *"The PUBLISH step is withheld by operator order O5."* O5 is recorded verbatim in the ruling table (`SPEC.md:83`) as **RELEASE LAW — v0.4.5 does not publish to PyPI**, with the `release-gate` environment approval left deliberately unapproved. Rejected alternative (c) is explicitly *"Publishing anyway because the pipeline is automated — the pipeline's `approve` job exists precisely so a human decides"*, which is the correct reading of a manual-approval gate as a control rather than an obstacle.

The ADR does not paper over the consequence: it records that the one-axis law's sentence becomes true of the **lineage** (`0.4.2 → 0.4.4`) and not of `HEAD` (`0.4.5`), names this the second such mint after the retired `0.4.3`, and routes the wording fix to memory at closure with an explicit revisit trigger. D6 (`SPEC.md:110-115`) states the mechanism once, including that **no `v0.4.5` git tag is created**.

Security reading: A16.8 turns the order into three verifiable post-conditions — `release.yml`'s `approve` job pending-unapproved, no `v0.4.5` tag, PyPI latest still `0.4.4`. No artifact reaches a public index without a human decision, and the absence of a tag means no release asset is mintable from this ship. Nothing to remediate.

findings.detail_md:
**Delta shape** (`git diff --name-status origin/main..199b356b`): `R100` `specs/releases/v0.4.4/verdicts/dfa2e95e….handoff.json` → `specs/_archive/releases/v0.4.4/verdicts/dfa2e95e….handoff.json` (rename, 0 content lines changed — the archive sweep the file's own `scope` field anticipated, executed by `git mv` as the FROZEN class requires); `M` BACKLOG.md (+94), bugs.jsonl (+1), ACTIVE.md (±2); `A` v0.4.5 SPEC.md (+694), PLAN.md (+248), TASKS.md (+1020). **No file under `dadaia_workspace/`, no `pyproject.toml`/lockfile, no `.github/**`, no Dockerfile/compose/Terraform** — so the CVE lane and the IaC lane have no input in this delta (`cve_findings: 0`, `new_dependencies: 0` are true by absence of a manifest, not by an unrun scan).

**Sweeps over the added lines** (`grep '^+'` on the specs diff → 2065 lines), each exit code read directly, no pipe:

| # | class | pattern | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | secret assignment | `(password|passwd|secret|token|api_key|apikey|private_key)\s*=\s*["'][^"']{6,}` | exit 1 — no match |
| 2 | PEM private key | `BEGIN (RSA|EC|OPENSSH|PGP|DSA)? ?PRIVATE KEY` | exit 1 — no match |
| 3 | home-absolute path | `/home/[a-z]`, `/Users/[a-z]`, `C:\\Users` | exit 1 — no match |
| 4 | email literal | RFC-ish address shape | exit 1 — no match |
| 5 | IPv4 / host literal | dotted quad, `https?://…\.(com|net|io|org)` | exit 1 — no match |
| 6 | cloud key / bearer | `AKIA…`, `gh[pousr]_…`, `sk-…`, `xox[baprs]-`, `Bearer …`, `eyJ….` | exit 1 — no match |

Supplementary passes for consumer-specific exposure (the recurring class): zero hits for private repo slugs and consumer product names, zero for operator personal-name tokens, zero for `.env`/`credentials`/`.pypirc`/`id_rsa`/`.pem`/`PYPI_*TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`/`AWS_*` filename or variable references.

**Push gate**, fed the real new-branch refspec on stdin with the exit read into a variable before any pipe: `refs/heads/feature/0.4.5 199b356b… refs/heads/feature/0.4.5 000…0` → `[pre-push] denylist scan mode: operator denylist + baseline`, **exit 0**, zero offenders — the operator denylist layer was loaded, so this is a substantive pass and not a no-op.

**Self-scan**: `tests/integration/test_repo_self_scan.py` → **5 passed**, run with `-p no:cacheprovider` so no cache artifact lands in the repo tree.

**Ledger event** added by the definition commit is clean and carries no path, host or free-text leak surface: `{"bug_id": "two-atomic-writers-leak-temp-file-on-injected-os-replace-failure", "event": "superseded", "reported_by": "software-engineer", "superseded_by": "atomic-write-primitive-consolidation", "ts": "…"}` — matching D4's requirement that the `superseded` event be appended in the definition commit.

**Bug-surface direction** (standing order): the delta is specs prose and changes no executed path, so it neither reduces nor increases the bug surface of any feature. The release it defines is declared net-negative in production LOC and AI-surface lines with FR16/A16.3/A16.4 as the acceptance, and its three deletion engines (FR2, FR4, FR13) each land `expand → switch → contract` per D7 — the correct direction under the standing order.
